19.0.s.en: 1. Attention to great and small things

19.0.0.en: 1 A laboring man that is a drunkard shall not be rich; and he that despiseth small things shall fall little by little. 2 Wine and women will make men of understanding to fall away. 3 And he that cleaveth to harlots will become impudent. Moths and worms shall have him to heritage, and the impudent soul shall be taken away. 4 He that is hasty to give credit is light-minded; and he that sinneth offendeth against his own soul. 5 Whoso taketh pleasure in wickedness shall be condemned; but he that hateth to be talked to lessens his sins.

19.0.1.en: He begins with negligence in drinking wine, while practical experience confirms that the life of the drunkard is filled with misery; negligence in improper bodily (sexual) matters is tragic, and association with fornicators corrupts a man's life. Negligence in these matters causes material loss, the misleading of the mind, loss of reputation, corruption of the body, instability of the soul, and falling under judgment. All this calls us to a healthy self-control.

19.0.2.en: A drunken laborer will not become rich, and he who despises small things will fall little by little [1].

19.0.3.en: The Apostle says: "Drink no longer water, but use a little wine for thy stomach's sake and thine often infirmities" (1 Tim 5:23). Wine was permitted within the narrowest limits as a medicine, and in some cold regions because of the bitter cold.

19.0.4.en: The scholar Tertullian says that Timothy [abstained from wine, not out of a rule, but because of his consecration.] Wine in itself is not forbidden by a rule, but it is unbecoming, especially for those consecrated to the service of the Lord. St. Clement of Alexandria sees that Timothy used wine as a tonic suited to his sick and weakened body. As for the emphasis on using "a little" of it, it was lest the sick forget themselves through much wine [1].

19.1.0.en: Some used it as a drink of hospitality, and within the narrowest limits, lest children become accustomed to it, and others without limits; but the Church preferred to forbid taking it, especially since abstaining from it does no harm to a person, whereas taking it may cause him to become addicted to it. The problem with wine is that when it brings the drinker to the point of drunkenness, he turns into another person, lacking dignity, balance and a sense of responsibility, and even unaware of the seriousness of drunkenness. It makes a person lose his covering and exposes him even before his own sons, as happened with Noah (Gen 9:21). St. Jerome says: [No one may say that drunkenness is not a sin; we read of Noah that he was drunk once, but God warns us not to suppose him a drunkard and an addict of wine [2].] He also says: [In one hour of drunkenness he was laid bare (Noah), who for six hundred years had remained covered with dignity [3].] He also says: [After his drunkenness his body was laid bare; for the pampering of the soul leads in the end to falling into lust: the belly is first gorged, and then the members rise up in revolt [4].] And St. Ambrose says: [O the power of wine! It made him whom the waters of the flood did not overcome to become naked! [5]]

19.2.0.en: v The monks were celebrating one of the feasts in Scetis, and they gave one of the elders a cup of wine, but he refused it, saying: "Take this death away from me." When the others who were eating with him saw what he had done, they too refused to take any of the wine [6].

19.2.1.en: Paradise of the Fathers The lust of drunkenness makes a man unable even to buy the food he needs. The wise man says that wine and dissolute women make a person overpowered (Prov 23:31-33).

19.3.0.en: He who controls himself does not squander his money in drunkenness, nor is he negligent even in small matters. St. Augustine says: "Faithfulness in small things is not a small matter." St. Augustine sees that our Lord Jesus often proclaims "Watch" (Mt 24:42; 25:13; 26:38, 41; Mk 13:37), and also says: "Walk while ye have the light, lest darkness come upon you" (Jn 12:35), since He keeps us from the gradual approach of the serpent, who instills evil in us [7].

19.4.0.en: v Let us not make light of our sins because they are small, but fear them because they are many. The drops of rain are small, but because they are many they can shake mountains [8].

19.4.1.en: Father Caesarius, bishop of Arles v Just as the water that gathers in the hold of a ship and rises gradually and imperceptibly has the same effect as if the ship were in the midst of a storm, so also the inflammations are small when the pustules appear scattered over the members of the body; but when they spread and cannot be counted, they may destroy life as if it were one great and dangerous wound afflicting the chest. Therefore we read what is written: "A laboring man that is a drunkard shall not be rich, and he that despiseth small things shall fall little by little." Those who neglect sorrow and repentance and do not avoid small sins not only fall from the state of righteousness, but descend little by little and far, until complete ruin.

19.5.0.en: v Those who constantly transgress with small sins should think well that sometimes the worst sins are committed in small matters rather than in greater ones. We recognize the greater sins more quickly, and so they can be healed more quickly. But the smaller sins we do not look at, nor do we even regard them as sins. Thus they grow and become worse, since we show little concern when committing them. Likewise it always happens that when the soul becomes accustomed to these small things, it no longer fears the great one among them [9].

19.6.0.en: v (St. Zosimas) added: St. Ignatius the God-bearer said: I need the meekness by which I destroy all the power of the ruler of this age. The sign of our renunciation of the world is that we are no longer troubled by anything. For it may happen that after a man has left millions, he becomes attached to a small needle with a sick attachment, so that he is troubled on its account. The needle has taken the place of the millions, and thus he becomes a slave to this needle, or to a cap, or to a garment, or to a book, and is no longer a slave of God! [10]

19.6.1.en: Paradise of the Fathers Wine and women lead the wise astray, and he who associates with fornicators becomes more unstable [2].

19.6.2.en: v The evil of drunkenness appears clearly in the case of Lot and his daughters. When he was drunk with wine he lay with his daughters and did not care about it. Pharaoh also, being drunk, hanged the baker on a cross.

19.7.0.en: Add to this the Jewish people, of whom we read: "The people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play" (Ex 32:6). They drank much wine, and afterward they asked for idols to be made, and in honoring these idols they began to dance, bending their limbs in frenzy with movements of every kind. Herod also, being inflamed with much wine, ordered the killing of St. John the Baptist as a reward for a single dance performed by a girl [11].

19.7.1.en: Father Caesarius, bishop of Arles Rot and worms shall inherit him, and his reckless soul shall be uprooted [3].

19.8.0.en: v By fornication are understood all bodily and animal lusts. Holy Scripture speaks of idolatry as fornication, and the Apostle Paul calls covetousness idolatry, and therefore it is fornication. So every evil lust is rightly called fornication, because the spirit is corrupted by leaving the lofty law that governs it and sells its honor for a base lust that does not befit the loftiness of the spirit [12]!

19.9.0.en: St. Augustine v The custom of marrying sisters ceased from the time of Abraham. And the contracting of marriage with many wives ceased from the days of the prophets. As we read: "Go not after thy lusts, but refrain thyself from thine appetites" (8:30). And in another place: "Let thy fountain be blessed, and rejoice with the wife of thy youth" (Prov 5:18), for it clearly forbids polygamy. And Jeremiah plainly gives the name of neighing horses to those who desire other men's wives [13].

19.10.0.en: Father Methodius v Above all it befits the monk also to abstain from the company of women and from drinking wine, for wine and women lead astray even the wise (see Sir 19:2) [14]

19.10.1.en: St. Basil the Great He who is quick to trust is not wise in heart, and he who sins is a criminal against himself [4].

19.11.0.en: v My heart rejoices in you, my dear son. May the eternal God and the Lord Jesus Christ guard you! Do not believe everyone, nor place your confidence in all, nor let anyone gain the upper hand over you through flattery and praise. There are many who serve Satan: "He that is hasty to give credit is light-minded..." (see Sir 19:4) [15].

19.11.1.en: St. Ignatius of Antioch He who rejoices in iniquity shall be condemned [5].

19.12.0.en: 6 He that sinneth against himself repenteth, and he that taketh pleasure in evil shall be condemned. 7 Repeat not that which is evil, and thou shalt lose nothing. 8 Whether it be to friend or foe, talk not of other men's lives; and if thou canst without offence, reveal them not. 9 For he heard and observed thee, and when time came he hated thee. 10 If thou hast heard a word, let it die with thee; and be bold, it will not burst thee. 11 A fool travaileth with a word, as a woman in labor of a child. 12 As an arrow that sticketh in the thigh of a fleshy man, so is a word within a fool's belly.

19.12.1.en: St. Mar Jacob of Serugh warns women as well as men against chattering in the holy Church. Control of the tongue requires not chattering, not passing on words to any person however much a friend of yours he may be, and keeping to caution and reserve. The proper use of the tongue is shown in the following: 1. Avoiding chatter keeps us from evil. 2. Being careful not to pass on to others what we hear, unless silence would mean harm, loss and injustice to a person! 3. Let our depths be like a grave in which we bury what we hear, lest we travail with a word that becomes the embryo of evil.

19.12.2.en: v The world met me bearing woes to distribute to me. My Lord, I will not take from its gift, which is full of harms.

19.12.3.en: In the world chatter and noise are acquired along with curses; give me Your word, that in its company I may find quiet.

19.12.4.en: It is a second sea, and behold, it troubles me with its storms. O Harbor of life, give me rest in Your pure place.

19.13.0.en: The world is mire, and he who goes down into it makes his soul stink. My Lord, by Your teaching wash me, for I am defiled by the world [16].

19.13.1.en: v The Pharisee, who was righteous according to the Law, became beautiful in his own eyes, and stood to recount his good deeds.

19.13.2.en: He looked at the tax collector, who had also gone up to pray, and despised him and rejected him, and directed mocking words at him.

19.13.3.en: He thanked the Lord with a spirit full of chatter, and compared himself with the tax collector, and found that he was greater than he.

19.14.0.en: He said: God, I thank You that I am not like this tax collector, for he forgot that it was a prayer (Lk 18:11) [17].

19.14.1.en: v Women sit in the holy temple of prayers (the Church), with their mouths gaping with excessive talk.

19.14.2.en: The prophets cry out to teach the earth good things, while they chatter with vain and unseemly news.

19.14.3.en: Satan himself blinds the eyes of men, and at every opportunity he tries to kill them.

19.14.4.en: The giant found that everyone whispers quietly in prayers between himself and the Lord, and in place of the course of prayers he put the whispers of vain news in the mouths of the women.

19.14.5.en: O wretched woman, whisper in prayer, and uncover your wound to the hidden Physician, who dresses the wound and does not expose it... The evil one wishes to disturb with chatter this work, which dresses the wounds of all sinners.

19.14.6.en: He makes a man chatter with his neighbor in the holy temple, to relate vain news without benefit.

19.14.7.en: Satan gathers and brings in some words from the leftovers that error has left in men.

19.15.0.en: He reminds you of words you had forgotten before you entered, so that you utter them at the time of prayers [18].

19.15.1.en: St. Mar Jacob of Serugh St. Mar Jacob of Serugh sees the tongue of the holy believer as a fruitful mother, who does not bear chatter but praises to God the Creator: 1. It does not cease to bring forth new praises, not in respect of the words, but in respect of their character as a hymn of love that never grows old. 2. The rock that followed the people in the wilderness poured out upon them flowing living waters; so the sanctified tongue brings forth rivers of living water. 3. It does not befit the tongue of the believer to be like the slothful servant who hid his master's silver in the earth and did not trade with it, so that it did not gain (Mt 25:14-30). 4. If the tongue ceases to praise, God calls the stones to praise Him, as happened on the day of His crucifixion, when men ceased to praise, and the sun and moon and earth and rocks and tombs set out to praise Him, each in its own language.

19.15.2.en: And he who hates chatter, his sin is lessened [6].

19.15.3.en: God did not create the tongue for chatter, but that we might place it in His hands, so that He sanctifies it and makes of it a spiritual harp on which His Holy Spirit plays a joyful symphony of love. God is concerned for man's tongue and offers it a heavenly guard, yet not by compulsion, but at man's request.

19.15.4.en: v Men were created to praise much, and perhaps they would remember praise every day in abundance! The shining sun does not shine for itself or run its course for itself, but it has light to give light to men.

19.15.5.en: And for their sake the luminaries (the stars) came to be in the atmosphere, and (the enlightened men) benefit from the days and the nights.

19.15.6.en: To men belong discernment, knowledge, the word and the voice, that they may give praise to the Most High in His place.

19.15.7.en: The mouth of man is made perfect, as though for the praise of the Lord, and he who ceases to praise becomes ungrateful.

19.15.8.en: And for this you have a mouth, that you may praise with it, give thanks with it, rejoice with it, and bless with it.

19.15.9.en: Praise, for you have the praising word; and rejoice, for you have the voice full of melodies.

19.15.10.en: Give thanks, for you have mind and discernment; and bless, for you have become a rational vessel and not a silent one.

19.15.11.en: You were nothing, and mercies made you something great... So give thanks with wonder; why are you silent?

19.16.0.en: Enter into yourself and look at your person within you, for in you are all the wonders of the creative power [19].

19.16.1.en: v My Lord, may the lowly mouth that rejoices in You and the tongue that chants Your praise, though unworthy, rejoice in You.

19.17.0.en: My Lord, may the speaker also rejoice in You, and the hearers, for You have gladdened them by Your birth; to You be praise [20].

19.18.0.en: v He made for him a mouth to praise the Lord his God, and through it he takes foods for his whole body [21].

19.18.1.en: St. Mar Jacob of Serugh Never repeat a word, and you will never be a loser [7].

19.18.2.en: Do not tell it to a friend or an enemy, and do not reveal it unless you would sin by keeping it [8].

19.18.3.en: Someone may hear you and guard against you, and hate you when the time comes [9].

19.18.4.en: Have you heard a word? Let it die with you.

19.18.5.en: Be bold! For it will not make you burst [10].

19.18.6.en: v You heard a word from a man while he was in a state of anger, pained and resentful; let the word die in you. Why do you repeat it? Why do you proclaim it? It does not tear you apart if you leave it inside you. In any case, speak with your friend who wishes to make you an enemy of another friend of yours. Speak with him and treat him with a soothing remedy, as for a sick soul.

19.18.7.en: Say to him: Why do you want me to become an enemy of that man? He may answer you: He is my enemy!

19.18.8.en: Say to him: Do you want me to be an enemy of your enemy? I want to be an enemy of your sin. The one whose enemy you want me to be is a man. There is an enemy of you both, and I must be his enemy if I am your friend.

19.18.9.en: He answers you: Who is this other enemy of mine?

19.18.12.en: - The hatred with which you hate your friend.

19.19.0.en: In this be a physician. For the physician does not love the sick man unless he hates his sickness. He fights against the fever to free the sick man from it. Do not love the vices of your friends, if you love them [22].

19.19.1.en: Father Caesarius, bishop of Arles v I do not know from where this disease fell upon men. We have become chatterers, keeping nothing in our minds. Hear the counsel of a wise man, who says: "Hast thou heard a word? Let it die with thee; and be bold, it will not burst thee" (see Sir 19:10). Again: "A fool travaileth with a word, as a woman in labor of a child" (see Sir 19:11). We are ready to bring accusations and prepared for condemnation. Even if we commit nothing else evil, this is enough to destroy us, and it carries us to hell, and occupies us with ten thousands of evils. And that you may know this for certain, hear what the prophet says: "Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother" (Ps 50:20).

19.19.2.en: St. John Chrysostom At a word like this the fool travails, as a woman in labor of a child [11].

19.19.3.en: As an arrow that sticketh in the flesh of the thigh, so is a word in the belly of a fool [12].

19.19.4.en: v Man is mortal in his body, but in his mind and his word he is immortal.

19.20.0.en: In silence you see your mind, but when you use your mind, you speak within yourself. For during silence the mind begets the word, and the word of thanksgiving offered to God is the salvation of man [23].

19.21.0.en: v He who speaks foolishly has no mind, for he speaks without thinking about all matters. Therefore examine what is useful for you, for the salvation of your soul, so that you may do it [24].

19.22.0.en: v The reasonable word that benefits the soul is a gift from God, but the empty word that merely investigates the measures of heaven and earth, and the distance between them, and the sizes of the sun and the stars, those who occupy themselves with that... are like those who draw water with a sieve, for men cannot discover (all) this [25].

19.23.0.en: 13 Admonish a friend, it may be he hath not done it; and if he have done it, that he do it no more. 14 Admonish thy friend, it may be he hath not said it; and if he have, that he speak it not again. 15 Admonish a friend, for many times it is a slander. 16 And believe not every tale. There is one that slippeth in his speech, but not from his heart. 17 And who is he that hath not offended with his tongue? Admonish thy neighbor before thou threaten him.

19.23.1.en: When you hear that someone is speaking about you something bad, it is advisable to speak with him directly in love and meekness, without speaking with others about what you heard.

19.23.2.en: Ask your friend, perhaps he did nothing, and if he did it, he may not do it again [13].

19.24.0.en: Ben Sira urges us to be careful in examining matters. In a spirit of love and wisdom, if he hears of a friend or neighbor who has spoken evil of him, he should examine the matter without agitation. With wisdom he should speak with the friend or neighbor so that he does not repeat it concerning anyone else. Let him always walk according to the Law of the Most High [17].

19.24.1.en: Ask your neighbor, perhaps he did not say anything, and if he said it, perhaps he will not repeat the saying [14].

19.24.2.en: Ask your friend, for it is often slander, and do not believe every word (you have heard) [15].

19.25.0.en: v If anyone accuses a person of having wronged him, may he not keep that in his mind, whether it was against his neighbor or against us. I ask of you a kindness, that you come to us, and present the accusation, and receive from us our defense of ourselves. It is said: "Ask him, lest what you heard about him he did not say. Ask him, lest he did not do (what you accuse him of). And if he did it, let him not repeat it." For we will either defend ourselves, or if we are at fault we will apologize and strive not to fall into the same errors. This is for your benefit and ours, for you may have accused us without cause, and when you know the truth of the matter you will correct what you supposed; and we, if we have wronged you without knowing, will mend our ways [26].

19.26.0.en: v "I will go down now, and see whether they have done altogether according to the cry of it, which is come unto me; and if not, I will know" (see Gen 18:21). What the Father says is this: "A report has come to me, but I wish once more to test this rumor more precisely in the light of the facts. I do not do this because I do not know whether I am doing it, but because I wish to teach men not to concern themselves with talk alone, nor to believe it carelessly if someone speaks it against another." It befits men to believe what they hear after they have made a careful examination and found proof in the light of the facts. This is the reason that God said in another place: "Believe not every tale" (see Sir 19:15). For nothing ruins the life of men like their believing everything that people say [27].

19.26.1.en: St. John Chrysostom A man may slip without intending to; and who is he that has not offended with his tongue? [16]

19.26.2.en: Ask your neighbor before you threaten him, and let the Law of the Most High take its course [17].

19.27.0.en: v We read in the Holy Scriptures, beloved, that good counsel preserves those who are eager for the salvation of their souls, as the divine word says: "Holy counsel shall preserve thee." If holy counsel preserves a soul, then unholy counsel not only fails to preserve it but kills it [28].

19.28.0.en: 18 And give place to the Law of the Most High. All wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and in all wisdom is the fulfilling of the Law. 19 But the knowledge of wickedness is not wisdom, neither at any time the counsel of sinners prudence. 20 There is a wickedness, and the same an abomination; and there is a fool wanting in wisdom. 21 He that hath small understanding, and feareth God, is better than one that hath much wisdom, and transgresseth the Law. 22 There is an exquisite subtlety, and the same is unjust. 23 And there is one that turneth aside to make judgment appear; and there is a wicked man that hangeth down his head sadly, but inwardly he is full of deceit. 24 Casting down his countenance, and making as if he heard not; where he is not known, he will do thee a mischief before thou be aware. 25 And if for want of power he be hindered from sinning, yet when he findeth opportunity he will do evil. 26 A man may be known by his look, and one that hath understanding by his countenance, when thou meetest him. 27 A man's attire, and excessive laughter, and gait, show what he is.

19.28.1.en: At some length Ben Sira warns us against the false appearances of wisdom, as a kind of cunning that works in the service of injustice and evil under the cover of deceptive appearances. It is not practiced in the fear of the Lord, and it does not care to keep the Law of the Lord practically and seriously from the depths of the heart.

19.28.2.en: All wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and in all wisdom is the fulfilling of the Law [18].

19.28.3.en: Wisdom does not stop at merely advising sinners. The wise man is committed to keeping the Law of the Lord and walks in the fear of the Lord.

19.29.0.en: The knowledge of wickedness is not wisdom, nor is discernment in the counsel of sinners [19].

19.29.1.en: v Those who are full of evil and whom ignorance has made drunk do not know God, for they are not lofty in spirit. But God is known only by the mind (that is, by the loftiness of our spiritual understanding), and although He is invisible, He is clearly perceived in the things that are seen, like the spirit that appears in the body. And just as the body cannot live without the spirit, so nothing visible and existing can subsist without God [29].

19.30.0.en: St. Anthony the Great There is a cleverness that is an abomination, and there is a fool who lacks wisdom [20].

19.31.0.en: It is better for a man to be ignorant but to keep himself from sin, than to have knowledge and misuse it. The man who fears (God) and lacks understanding is better than he who has abundant prudence and transgresses the Law [21].

19.32.0.en: There is an exquisite skill and yet it is unjust, and there is a man who deceives to establish his right [22].

19.33.0.en: There is a wicked man who walks bowed down in sorrow, while his inward part is full of deceit [23].

19.34.0.en: He hides his face and pretends to be deaf, and when no one is aware of him he overcomes you [24].

19.35.0.en: And if he is prevented from wrongdoing because he lacks strength, he does evil afterward when the opportunity comes to him [25].

19.35.1.en: v Many have the appearance of humility, but they do not have the virtue. Many present the appearance on the outside, but within they fight against it. They put on a play of humility, but they reject the truth, because "there is a wicked man that goeth bowed down under the weight of evil, but inwardly he is full of deceit" (see Sir 19:23). Such a person is very far from humility [30].

19.35.2.en: St. Ambrose Truly it befits us to concentrate on our inner life, because it is reflected in our outward conduct. At the same time we do not ignore the outward appearance, for it too can reveal the inner wisdom.

19.36.0.en: A man is known by his appearance, and the wise man is known by the features of his face when you meet him [26].

19.37.0.en: A man's clothing, and the way he laughs and walks, indicate who he is [27].

19.37.1.en: Seriousness with gentleness in all appearances, dress and movements, even the way of walking and laughing, reveals the character of a man. It does not befit the wise man to behave like a buffoon or a jester.

19.37.2.en: The true believer does not need anyone to bear witness to his godliness and conduct in Christ Jesus; rather even his outward appearance or his holy body language, such as his dress, his smile and his way of walking, bears witness for him while he is silent. For the true Christian is distinguished from others, sanctified within and in his outward conduct.

19.37.3.en: v The true prudence of the soul and its virtue appear in a man's glances, his way of walking, his voice, his smile, his conversation and his manners. For everything in such a soul has been changed and has become the best it can be, and its thought, which loves God, becomes a watchful guard over it, preventing the entry of evil, shameful thoughts [31].

19.37.4.en: St. Anthony the Great v Once we are inscribed in the spiritual assembly of the Church, we rightly do not allow ourselves to practice the same deeds that others practice, but always show the control of our tongue and the purity of our mind, and our members learn not to undertake any work that is not profitable for the soul.

19.37.5.en: What shall I say? We use the tongue only in praises and thanksgiving and in reading the divine commandments and spiritual conversations. As it is said: "Let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth, but that which is good to the use of edifying, that it may minister grace unto the hearers. And grieve not the Holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed" (Eph 4:29-30). Do you know that if you fail in this you grieve the Holy Spirit? Therefore I ask you to try not to do anything that grieves the Holy Spirit.

19.37.6.en: If we must go out, let us not take part in dangerous gatherings that go beyond all bounds and are full of folly.

19.37.7.en: Rather, prefer nothing to the Church of God, the houses of prayer, and discussion in spiritual gatherings. Let every work be extremely dignified. As it is said: "A man's attire, and laughter of the mouth, and gait, show what he is" (see Sir 19:27). The outward appearance shows clearly the state of the soul. Truly the movement of the member proclaims its beauty in a certain way... "If any man be in Christ, he is a new creature" (2 Cor 5:17) [32].

19.37.8.en: St. John Chrysostom v Let her glances, her love, her speech, her way of walking and her dress tell of virtue [33].

19.38.0.en: 28 There is one that reproveth, and it is not comely; and there is one that holdeth his tongue, and he is wise.

19.38.1.en: (The commentary is in the next chapter) (*).

19.39.s.en: My depths cry out to You: Sanctify me completely!

19.39.0.en: v To You, O Holy One, I complain of myself; who can control my depths but You?!

19.39.1.en: Grant me not to be careless in what I count as small things, lest I be careless also in the great!

19.39.2.en: You have set me up as a holy temple in which Your Holy Spirit dwells.

19.39.3.en: Let Him be my sanctifier, and my keeper and guard.

19.39.4.en: Who will keep me from what is wrongly called the white lie?

19.39.5.en: And who will grant me seriousness, so that I am not drawn to a word of jesting, and no mockery slips from my tongue by way of playfulness.

19.39.6.en: You paid Your precious blood as the price for sanctifying every thought or word or movement, hidden or manifest.

19.39.7.en: v Grant me not to be careless and drink a cup of wine on one occasion or another.

19.39.8.en: Our father Noah celebrated the new world that the flood had washed.

19.39.9.en: He drank wine to excess and was laid bare; and his son Ham made light of him, he whom he had rescued together with his two brothers Shem and Japheth and the rest of the family.

19.39.10.en: Let Your Holy Spirit pour out His joy in my heart, so that I do not share with Noah in his drunkenness, but share with the heavenly hosts in their praises full of jubilation.

19.39.11.en: v Samson, who killed a lion without a weapon, and enjoyed honey from the lion's carcass, he and his parents, dallied with Delilah, and became lowly before the enemies, grinding like an ox; they put out his eyes, and he realized that he had lost his inner sight.

19.39.12.en: Grant me seriousness, so that I may have no wrongful familiarity under the cover of innocent kindness.

19.39.13.en: v Grant me wisdom from You, so that I do not choose a friend for myself without examination and study!

19.39.14.en: You have made my heart a treasury in which You deposit Your divine secrets; let me not leave its door open without heavenly guard.

19.39.15.en: v Let me hide in You, O Way, Truth and Life, so that I do not walk in the way of sinners, nor take part in the seat of the scornful.

19.39.16.en: Let me not open my mouth in frivolity in talking with one fallen in sin, but keep to Your dwelling in my heart and my mind, so that I utter no word unbecoming to Your son, nor distort the features of my face by playing with a reckless person!

19.39.17.en: v Who will sanctify my tongue to be like a mother that bears praises and thanksgivings, that praises You continually with the new song.

19.39.18.en: Let my tongue bear sweet words that carry the sweetness of Your commandments.

19.39.19.en: And let it not bear the chatter of vain speech that has no benefit.

19.39.20.en: Your Holy Spirit plays upon all my strings:

19.39.21.en: the tongue, the heart, the mind, the senses and the emotions, so that a symphony of love comes forth, which a fragrance of pleasure breathes in.

19.39.22.en: v Grant me wisdom from You, so that my silence together with my words may reveal Your work in me!

19.39.23.en: Let there be no place for folly in my depths, so that I do not practice vain or corrupt silence, nor let unseemly words come out of my mouth!

19.39.24.en: Let me hide in You, so that I do not respond to words that I hear hastily, but meet You continually, for You are my divine Counselor.

19.39.25.en: If a man tells me that his brother wronged me by speaking slanderously about me, with deliberation I will admonish my brother, not that he may apologize to me, but that he may be filled with love, meekness and gentleness.

19.39.26.en: If he confesses his fault, I will pray for him and for myself, that the Lord may purify us all from every weakness and sin.

19.39.27.en: v Truly I cry out: In Your light I see light. Reveal to me Your secrets, for I wish to see You, and to know Your wonderful plan, Your love and Your care.

19.39.28.en: I wish to keep Your commandments, and enjoy their sweet yoke, so that I may prepare for the day of my meeting with You!

19.39.29.en: Grant Your commandments to shine forth in my thoughts and emotions and in my hidden and outward conduct; Your commandments lead even my smile and the manner of my eating, drinking, sleeping and recreation.

19.39.30.en: v Grant me not to judge anyone by his outward conduct, for no one knows what is in his heart but You.
